signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY price action is anchored by a significant G10 bilateral theme, with CAD outperforming peers by +0.677% while JPY remains the G10 laggard at -0.766%. The leader-to-laggard spread has widened to 1.443%, reflecting a regime of CAD strength and JPY structural weakness. This divergence is fundamentally supported by a +125bp OIS carry advantage for the CAD, alongside a positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +12.0 for Canada vs the JPY's +13.8. BoJ holds at 1.0%. Trade bias: Bullish CAD/JPY; strong G10 outperformance and carry advantage favor continuation. Catalyst: RBA meeting 11 Aug — potential for cross-carry read-across. Risk: Sudden risk-off sentiment spikes VIX above 25, triggering a disorderly JPY carry unwind.

signals.title: USD/JPY — COT vs Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.11 is holding below its SMA20/50 cluster (161.08/161.16) but remains above the SMA200 at 158.09. Speculative positioning shows a crowded JPY net short of -63,633 (COT LF), driven by the persistent +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage. However, the options market is pricing in significant downside risk, with 1M 25d Risk Reversals at -2.18—a strong put skew indicating high demand for JPY protection. This positioning vs options divergence suggests that while carry-seekers remain short JPY, institutional hedgers are aggressively paying for downside protection near the 160.00 psychological level. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish USD/JPY; crowded shorts and extreme options skew signal reversal risk near 160.00. Catalyst: US CPI release this week. Risk: Hawkish Fed commentary from officials like Hammack sustains the carry bid and invalidates the options-based downside hedge.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT Positioning vs OIS Pricing
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7061, maintaining a position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7009/0.6998/0.6928). COT data shows LF net long positioning at +37,990 (72.1% long), indicating a crowded bullish sentiment among speculators. This positioning now faces headwinds as high-impact headlines suggest softer Australian inflation is cooling RBA hike bets, despite a current -73bp OIS carry premium favoring the AUD. If the RBA strikes a neutral tone at today's meeting, the crowded spec long is vulnerable to a profit-taking unwind. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD; crowded long positioning and cooling hike bets create downside asymmetry. Catalyst: RBA meeting 11 Aug — 4.35% hold priced. Risk: RBA surprises with hawkish 'fine print' regarding persistent service inflation, validating the spec long.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3512, supported by its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.342/1.336/1.340. The pair exhibits a significant Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) of +5.0%, with ATM implied volatility at 11.0% against a 30-day realized volatility of only 6.0%. This elevated premium indicates the options market is pricing in substantial forward-looking risk compared to recent price action, likely due to US CPI jitters and Middle East tensions. While the spot remains bid and carry is neutral (0bp), the high cost of protection suggests institutional caution ahead of this week's US macro data. Trade bias: Long GBP/USD; trend-following with SMA support, but expensive vol caps aggressive upside conviction. Catalyst: US CPI next week. Risk: Sharp correction below SMA200 at 1.3408 forces a rapid vol mean-reversion and long liquidation.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance vs Positioning
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5887 is trading above its SMA20/50/200 cluster, buoyed by the strongest Economic Surprise Index (ESI) in the G10 at +24.4. This data outperformance stands in stark contrast to speculative positioning, which remains net short at -30,785 (9.7% long). Speculators have been fading NZD strength even as realized data consistently beats expectations. While the RBNZ real rate is accommodative at -1.56%, the disconnect between strong domestic data and crowded short positioning suggests a high-probability short-squeeze setup if upcoming data remains robust. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; data-led outperformance against a crowded spec short. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — Hike bias. Risk: Global risk-off sentiment leads to a US Dollar haven bid, overwhelming the local data outperformance.
